rationale: The workflow is a single-job scheduled broken-link check (workflow_dispatch plus a weekly schedule) with no matrix, no package installation, no build tool, and no test steps. The only workflow_yaml-scoped pattern with measured evidence is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout), but its precondition—representative successful-duration history—is not met: the CI history shows five consecutive schedule failures and no successful runs, so a safe timeout value cannot be derived and an arbitrary limit risks truncating valid runs and losing coverage. Other patterns are inapplicable: P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has no dependency installation to cache; P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT, P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, and the P-LIT-BAZEL-* patterns require a matrix, tests, or Bazel that this workflow lacks; P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW, P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, and P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE are ci_service-scoped or contraindicated (idle schedule is contraindicated because link checking depends on external links); P-LIT-ENV-CACHE, P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS, P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS, P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP, P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE, P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE, P-LIT-SMELL-REPAIR, and P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION have no matching inputs, outputs, environments, or configuration smells. No supported optimization is applicable.
